question.text: Which of the following is the graph of $y= -\sqrt{x}-1?$
question.explanation:
To obtain the graph of $y=-\sqrt{x}-1,$ we can perform the following transformations:

  • Take the graph of $y=\sqrt{x}.$

  • Reflect the graph in the $x$-axis to get the graph of $y=-\sqrt{x}.$

The result is the solid blue curve shown below.

  • Translate the result down by $1$ unit to get the graph of $y=-\sqrt{x}-1.$

The result is the solid blue curve shown below.

example.title: Graphing a Reflected Square Root Function Containing One Translation

question.text: Which of the following is the graph of $y=\sqrt{x-2}-2?$
question.explanation:
To obtain the graph of $y=\sqrt{x-2}-2,$ we can perform the following transformations:

  • Take the graph of $y=\sqrt{x}.$

  • Translate the graph to the right by $2$ units to get the graph of $y=\sqrt{x-2}.$

  • Translate the result down by $2$ units to get the graph of $y=\sqrt{x-2}-2.$

The result is the solid blue curve shown below.

example.title: Identifying a Square Root Function Containing Two Translations

question.text: The graph above is a translation of $y=\sqrt{x}.$ Identify the equation that generated the graph.
question.explanation:
To obtain the given graph, we can perform the following transformations:

  • Take the graph of $y=\sqrt{x}.$

  • Translate the graph to the right by $3$ units to get the graph of $y=\sqrt{x-3}.$

  • Translate the result up by $2$ units to get the graph of $y=\sqrt{x-3}+2.$

The result is the solid blue curve shown below.

Therefore, the correct answer is $y=\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\sqrt{x-3}+2}.$
